audit_status.review_note: Reviewed as continuation of Eliphaz's first speech: appeal to discipline, divine reversal motifs, rescue promises, and restoration formula. Preserved as Eliphaz's counsel, not final endorsement.

verses.restored: Call now; is there anyone who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?

familiar.text: Call now, if there be any that will answer thee; and to which of the saints wilt thou turn?

modern.text: “Call out if you please, but who will answer? To which of the holy ones will you turn?

original.text: קְֽרָא נָ֭א הֲיֵ֣שׁ עוֹנֶ֑ךָּ וְאֶל מִ֖י מִקְּדֹשִׁ֣ים תִּפְנֶֽה

verses.restored: For vexation kills the fool, and jealousy puts the simple to death.

familiar.text: For wrath killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the silly one.

modern.text: For resentment kills a fool, and envy slays the simple.

original.text: כִּֽי לֶֽ֭אֱוִיל יַהֲרָג כָּ֑עַשׂ וּ֝פֹתֶ֗ה תָּמִ֥ית קִנְאָֽה

verses.restored: I have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly I cursed his dwelling.

familiar.text: I have seen the foolish taking root: but suddenly I cursed his habitation.

modern.text: I have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly his house was cursed.

original.text: אֲֽנִי רָ֭אִיתִי אֱוִ֣יל מַשְׁרִ֑ישׁ וָאֶקּ֖וֹב נָוֵ֣הוּ פִתְאֹֽם

verses.restored: His children are far from safety, crushed in the gate, with no rescuer.

familiar.text: His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, neither is there any to deliver them.

modern.text: His sons are far from safety, crushed in court without a defender.

original.text: יִרְחֲק֣וּ בָנָ֣יו מִיֶּ֑שַׁע וְיִֽדַּכְּא֥וּ בַ֝שַּׁ֗עַר וְאֵ֣ין מַצִּֽיל

verses.restored: The hungry eat his harvest, taking it even from among thorns, and the thirsty pant after his wealth.

familiar.text: Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, and taketh it even out of the thorns, and the robber swalloweth up their substance.

modern.text: The hungry consume his harvest, taking it even from the thorns, and the thirsty pant after his wealth.

original.text: אֲשֶׁ֤ר קְצִיר֨וֹ רָ֘עֵ֤ב יֹאכֵ֗ל וְאֶֽל מִצִּנִּ֥ים יִקָּחֵ֑הוּ וְשָׁאַ֖ף צַמִּ֣ים חֵילָֽם

verses.restored: For trouble does not come out from dust, and harm does not sprout from the ground.

familiar.text: Although affliction cometh not forth of the dust, neither doth trouble spring out of the ground;

modern.text: For distress does not spring from the dust, and trouble does not sprout from the ground.

original.text: כִּ֤י לֹא יֵצֵ֣א מֵעָפָ֣ר אָ֑וֶן וּ֝מֵאֲדָמָ֗ה לֹא יִצְמַ֥ח עָמָֽל

verses.restored: But humanity is born to trouble, as sparks fly upward.

familiar.text: Yet man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward.

modern.text: Yet man is born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.

original.text: כִּֽי אָ֭דָם לְעָמָ֣ל יוּלָּ֑ד וּבְנֵי רֶ֝֗שֶׁף יַגְבִּ֥יהוּ עֽוּף

verses.restored: But I myself would seek the Divine, and to the Divine I would set my case,

familiar.text: I would seek unto God, and unto God would I commit my cause:

modern.text: However, if I were you, I would appeal to God and lay my cause before Him—

original.text: אוּלָ֗ם אֲ֭נִי אֶדְרֹ֣שׁ אֶל אֵ֑ל וְאֶל אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים אָשִׂ֥ים דִּבְרָתִֽי

verses.restored: who does great things beyond searching, wonders without number.

familiar.text: Which doeth great things and unsearchable; marvellous things without number:

modern.text: the One who does great and unsearchable things, wonders without number.

original.text: עֹשֶׂ֣ה גְ֭דֹלוֹת וְאֵ֣ין חֵ֑קֶר נִ֝פְלָא֗וֹת עַד אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר

verses.restored: He gives rain on the face of the earth and sends waters on the face of the fields.

familiar.text: Who giveth rain upon the earth, and sendeth waters upon the fields:

modern.text: He gives rain to the earth and sends water upon the fields.

original.text: הַנֹּתֵ֣ן מָ֭טָר עַל פְּנֵי אָ֑רֶץ וְשֹׁ֥לֵֽחַ מַ֝יִם עַל פְּנֵ֥י חוּצֽוֹת

verses.restored: He sets the lowly on high, and those who mourn are lifted to safety.

familiar.text: To set up on high those that be low; that those which mourn may be exalted to safety.

modern.text: He sets the lowly on high, so that mourners are lifted to safety.

original.text: לָשׂ֣וּם שְׁפָלִ֣ים לְמָר֑וֹם וְ֝קֹדְרִ֗ים שָׂ֣גְבוּ יֶֽשַׁע

verses.restored: He frustrates the schemes of the crafty, so their hands do not perform success.

familiar.text: He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise.

modern.text: He thwarts the schemes of the crafty, so that their hands find no success.

original.text: מֵ֭פֵר מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת עֲרוּמִ֑ים וְֽלֹא תַעֲשֶׂ֥ינָה יְ֝דֵיהֶ֗ם תּוּשִׁיָּֽה

verses.restored: He catches the wise in their craftiness, and the counsel of the twisted is hurried away.

familiar.text: He taketh the wise in their own craftiness: and the counsel of the froward is carried headlong.

modern.text: He catches the wise in their craftiness, and sweeps away the plans of the cunning.

original.text: לֹכֵ֣ד חֲכָמִ֣ים בְּעָרְמָ֑ם וַעֲצַ֖ת נִפְתָּלִ֣ים נִמְהָֽרָה

verses.restored: By day they meet darkness, and at noon they grope as in the night.

familiar.text: They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope in the noonday as in the night.

modern.text: They encounter darkness by day and grope at noon as in the night.

original.text: יוֹמָ֥ם יְפַגְּשׁוּ חֹ֑שֶׁךְ וְ֝כַלַּ֗יְלָה יְֽמַשְׁשׁ֥וּ בַֽצָּהֳרָֽיִם

verses.restored: He saves from the sword of their mouth, and from the hand of the strong, the needy.

familiar.text: But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.

modern.text: He saves the needy from the sword in their mouth and from the clutches of the powerful.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣שַׁע מֵ֭חֶרֶב מִפִּיהֶ֑ם וּמִיַּ֖ד חָזָ֣ק אֶבְיֽוֹן

verses.restored: So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.

familiar.text: So the poor hath hope, and iniquity stoppeth her mouth.

modern.text: So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.

original.text: וַתְּהִ֣י לַדַּ֣ל תִּקְוָ֑ה וְ֝עֹלָ֗תָה קָ֣פְצָה פִּֽיהָ

verses.restored: Look, blessed is the human whom the Divine corrects; therefore do not reject the discipline of Shaddai.

familiar.text: Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty:

modern.text: Blessed indeed is the man whom God corrects; so do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.

original.text: הִנֵּ֤ה אַשְׁרֵ֣י אֱ֭נוֹשׁ יוֹכִחֶ֣נּֽוּ אֱל֑וֹהַּ וּמוּסַ֥ר שַׁ֝דַּ֗י אַל תִּמְאָֽס

verses.restored: For he causes pain and binds up; he wounds, and his hands heal.

familiar.text: For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.

modern.text: For He wounds, but He also binds; He strikes, but His hands also heal.

original.text: כִּ֤י ה֣וּא יַכְאִ֣יב וְיֶחְבָּ֑שׁ יִ֝מְחַ֗ץ וידו תִּרְפֶּֽינָה

verses.restored: From six troubles he will rescue you; in seven, harm will not touch you.

familiar.text: He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.

modern.text: He will rescue you from six calamities; no harm will touch you in seven.

original.text: בְּשֵׁ֣שׁ צָ֭רוֹת יַצִּילֶ֑ךָּ וּבְשֶׁ֓בַע לֹא יִגַּ֖ע בְּךָ֣ רָֽע

verses.restored: In famine he will ransom you from death, and in war from the hand of the sword.

familiar.text: In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword.

modern.text: In famine He will redeem you from death, and in battle from the stroke of the sword.

original.text: בְּ֭רָעָב פָּֽדְךָ֣ מִמָּ֑וֶת וּ֝בְמִלְחָמָ֗ה מִ֣ידֵי חָֽרֶב

verses.restored: From the lash of the tongue you will be hidden, and you will not fear devastation when it comes.

familiar.text: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue: neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh.

modern.text: You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, and will not fear havoc when it comes.

original.text: בְּשׁ֣וֹט לָ֭שׁוֹן תֵּחָבֵ֑א וְֽלֹא תִירָ֥א מִ֝שֹּׁ֗ד כִּ֣י יָבֽוֹא

verses.restored: At devastation and hunger you will laugh, and of the wild animals of the earth you will not be afraid.

familiar.text: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh: neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth.

modern.text: You will laugh at destruction and famine, and need not fear the beasts of the earth.

original.text: לְשֹׁ֣ד וּלְכָפָ֣ן תִּשְׂחָ֑ק וּֽמֵחַיַּ֥ת הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ אַל תִּירָֽא

verses.restored: For with the stones of the field will be your covenant, and the wild animals of the field will be at peace with you.

familiar.text: For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field: and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.

modern.text: For you will have a covenant with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you.

original.text: כִּ֤י עִם אַבְנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֣ה בְרִיתֶ֑ךָ וְחַיַּ֥ת הַ֝שָּׂדֶ֗ה הָשְׁלְמָה לָֽךְ

verses.restored: You will know that your tent is peace; you will inspect your dwelling and miss nothing.

familiar.text: And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle shall be in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin.

modern.text: You will know that your tent is secure, and find nothing amiss when inspecting your home.

original.text: וְֽ֭יָדַעְתָּ כִּי שָׁל֣וֹם אָהֳלֶ֑ךָ וּֽפָקַדְתָּ֥ נָ֝וְךָ וְלֹ֣א תֶחֱטָֽא

verses.restored: You will know that your seed is many, and your offspring like the grass of the earth.

familiar.text: Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth.

modern.text: You will know that your offspring will be many, your descendants like the grass of the earth.

original.text: וְֽ֭יָדַעְתָּ כִּי רַ֣ב זַרְעֶ֑ךָ וְ֝צֶאֱצָאֶ֗יךָ כְּעֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: You will come to the grave in full vigor, like a stack of grain lifted up in its season.

familiar.text: Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season.

modern.text: You will come to the grave in full vigor, like a sheaf of grain gathered in season.

original.text: תָּב֣וֹא בְכֶ֣לַח אֱלֵי קָ֑בֶר כַּעֲל֖וֹת גָּדִ֣ישׁ בְּעִתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Look, this we have searched out; so it is. Hear it, and know it for yourself.

familiar.text: Lo this, we have searched it, so it is; hear it, and know thou it for thy good.

modern.text: Indeed, we have investigated, and it is true! So hear it and know for yourself.”

original.text: הִנֵּה זֹ֭את חֲקַרְנ֥וּהָ כֶּֽן הִ֑יא שְׁ֝מָעֶ֗נָּה וְאַתָּ֥ה דַֽע לָֽךְ
